origin: proposed in SOURCE_DROP.md as a triad harness; the dial vector, shadow protocol, interior-calibration checklist and pedigree format are the drop's, the design corrections in shadow_design.py are not
principle: A claim is only as strong as the weakest calibration in the chain. Every experiment has three agents, and the reasoning agent is an instrument like the other two.

agent_meaning.physical: the system being studied. Its state drifts with temperature, load and history.
agent_meaning.instrument: the thing producing numbers. Calibrated and traceable, or not.
agent_meaning.reasoning: the thing interpreting numbers, human or AI. Has its own gain, and it is usually unread.

instrument.high: full metrological chain, traceable, environmental compensation

reasoning.high: full mechanism reconstruction, multiple hypotheses, adversarial check

physical.check: system state declared: temperature, load, history

physical.note: shadow_design.py section 4: a run that revises the physical declaration reports a PHYSICAL finding, not a reasoning-dial gradient. Without this field the two are scored as the same thing.

instrument.check: instrument records independently of the observer reading it
instrument.note: shadow_design.py section 3: without an independent log, observer error is inferred from consensus and the skip condition cannot fail.

reasoning.check: human: emotional investment in a particular result
AI: model version, thinking budget, temperature, context window
conflict of interest declared: do I want this result?

readability_note: Three of the four reasoning checks are self-report, and a self-report from a miscalibrated observer is the quantity in question. That is reasoning-dial/CLAIM_TABLE.md RD_009 restated. Checks tied to something outside the observer -- ambient temperature, hours since sleep, a timestamp, a model version string -- are readable; the rest are declarations, and the pedigree marks which is which.

shadow_protocol.purpose: measure how much of a conclusion is a property of the observer rather than of the system
shadow_protocol.design: 2^3 factorial over the three dials at low/high
shadow_protocol.design_note: NOT one-factor-at-a-time. shadow_design.py section 1: OFAT cannot estimate an interaction at any number of runs, and the cross-gradient the playground exists to measure IS an interaction. Eight runs recover every main effect and every interaction exactly.
shadow_protocol.sealing: each shadow commits its reading before any other shadow's is revealed
shadow_protocol.sealing_note: shadow_design.py section 2: unsealed shadows anchor on each other and their agreement measures nothing. ../divergence-playground/ implements the seal, the three spread axes, and the null ensemble.
shadow_protocol.null_required: the disagreement between two runs of the SAME observer at the SAME dial, measured before any cross-observer spread is interpreted
shadow_protocol.blind_spot: consensus is blind to error the shadows share. Shadows reading one declaration through one prompt share most of their error.

panel_independence.rule: require a minimum N_eff over the shadow panel, not a minimum shadow COUNT
panel_independence.n_eff: participation ratio of the shadow correlation spectrum, (sum L)^2 / sum L^2
panel_independence.why: shadow_panel.py: a panel of four shadows can carry N_eff = 1.2. Counting shadows measures effort; the participation ratio measures how much of it was independent. ../model-ecology/phylogeny.py already computes this statistic for a family of estimators.
panel_independence.v1_gap: v1 requires human_baseline + ai_low + ai_high. On one model, ai_low and ai_high share a family bias and are close to one shadow at two dial settings -- so the human is the only decorrelated element, and dropping it takes N_eff from 1.61 to 1.14 and the false-pass rate from 38% to 84%.
panel_independence.without_a_human: supported, but the substitution is THREE MODEL FAMILIES, not three budgets on one model. Four families with no human reach N_eff 2.18 and false-pass 12.4%, stronger than v1's required panel with one. Adding a human on top of that changes N_eff by -0.02.
panel_independence.what_a_human_still_uniquely_supplies: embodied context. Cold-stiffened proprioception is not a failure mode any model has, which argues for a human shadow on physical measurements specifically -- a different argument from the decorrelation one.

consensus_denominator.v1_rule: 'Variance must be compared against instrument resolution, not against zero.'
consensus_denominator.verdict: an improvement over comparing to zero, and still the wrong denominator
consensus_denominator.correct_denominator: the same-observer repeat variance -- the spread of one observer measuring twice at one dial
consensus_denominator.why: instrument resolution bounds what the INSTRUMENT can say. Shadow spread is bounded by what an OBSERVER can repeat. If observer repeat variance exceeds instrument resolution, every panel reads 'exceeds_resolution' and the verdict is about the observer's repeatability, not about underdetermination.

pedigree_fields.layer_note: extends the three layers in ../reasoning-gate/guards.json with a fourth. A quantity whose value depends on who read it is reasoning-level, and a physical-scope claim resting on one is qualified, not supported -- the same rule gate.py already applies to generator-level support.
pedigree_fields.gate_verdict: per-guard result from ../reasoning-gate/, recorded with the number and inseparable from it

skip_conditions.rule: a skip condition must be able to fail
skip_conditions.test: state the outcome that would prevent the skip, and check the instrument can resolve it
skip_conditions.note: shadow_design.py section 3: 'all four observers agree within instrument resolution' fires whatever the truth is, because observers reading one dial agree to within a division by construction. That is null-harness's CONSTANT_SILENT.

based_on: spec_v1.json / SPEC_V1.md, checked in verbatim. This file is v1 plus the corrections in CLAIM_TABLE.md; where the two differ, the difference is a finding, not a preference.
gate_mapping_note: v1 section 6 assigns G-DIM the job of 'checks that dial settings are actually different compute levels'. G-DIM in ../reasoning-gate/guards.json voids ratios across unlike objects and does not do this. The job named is real and unassigned: nothing verifies that ai_low and ai_high actually produced different reasoning effort, and a model that ignores its budget parameter would collapse two declared shadows into one silently.
